title: Challenge: a task API
idea: A task API is a server that keeps tasks in memory and lets clients list, add and remove them over HTTP. You build one with `node:http` alone.

analogy.text: A whiteboard by the door. Visitors read it, ask you to add a line, or ask you to wipe one off. Only you hold the pen.
analogy.breaks: A whiteboard stays on the wall; server memory is lost when the process stops.

points: Start with a `404` for everything, then add one route per test run.
Match method and path together; split `/tasks/7` on `/` to get the id.
Ids come from a counter, because list length repeats an id after a delete.
Export `server` without calling `listen`; the tests listen on port `0` themselves.

hero.title: A task's life through the API

messages.label: POST /tasks {"title":"Buy tea"}
messages.note: The client sends JSON. The handler reads the body, checks `title`, stores a task and gives it the next id.

messages.label: 201 {id, title, done:false}
messages.note: `201` means created. The reply is the new task, and `done` starts as `false`.

messages.label: POST /tasks {}
messages.note: A second request arrives with no `title` at all.

messages.label: 400 + error message
messages.note: `400`: the request is wrong. The handler stops before it stores anything.

messages.label: GET /tasks
messages.note: A read changes nothing. The handler replies with the whole list.

messages.label: 200 [one task]
messages.note: `200` and a JSON array. Only task 1 exists; the refused request left no trace.

messages.label: DELETE /tasks/1
messages.note: The id arrives in the path as the string `'1'`. Convert it before comparing.

messages.label: 204, no body
messages.note: `204` means success with nothing to send back. Task 1 is gone.

messages.label: DELETE /tasks/1
messages.note: The client repeats the same call.

messages.label: 404 + error message
messages.note: Task 1 no longer exists, so the answer is `404`. Nothing changes.

code.title: Reading the tests
code.caption: The tests judge each reply with these calls: `equal` for values, `deepEqual` for objects. Strict mode never converts types.

code.title: Choosing an id
code.caption: Run it, then change `shift()` to `pop()`. Which way of choosing an id stays safe?

challenges.intro: Use only `node:http`. Each test prints one line, so you can watch `FAIL` turn into `ok` as you add routes.

items.title: Native task server
items.prompt: `GET /tasks` returns all tasks. `POST /tasks` creates `{id, title, done: false}` (201); bad JSON or a missing or empty `title` gives 400. `DELETE /tasks/:id` gives 204, or 404 if unknown. Anything else: 404 JSON.
hints: Make `GET /tasks` pass first. Read the path with `new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost').pathname`, check the method, then send the list.
For `POST`, join the body chunks and parse them in `try/catch`. Reject anything but a non-empty string `title`; take ids from a counter.
For `DELETE`, convert the text after `/tasks/` with `Number` and remove that task. Reply 204 if it existed; otherwise let the final 404 answer.

pitfalls: Do not call `server.listen` in your file; the tests listen, and a second call throws.
Answer `404`, not `405`, for other methods here: every unmatched request gets the same reply.
Check the id exists before `splice`; an index of `-1` removes the last task.

quiz.why: `split` returns strings, so `id` is `'2'`. Strict equality never converts, so `2 === '2'` is false and `findIndex` gives `-1`; `String(t.id)` matches at index 1.

takeaway: Pin down each route's method, path and status, then let the tests judge.

starters: Why must my file export `server` instead of calling `listen`?
Should deleting a task that does not exist be 404 or 204?
How would I add `PATCH /tasks/:id` to mark a task done?
